name: AI reply policy for bridged chats (opt-in bot mode)
description:
## Context
Bridging messenger ↔ WhatsApp is a mirror, not necessarily a chatbot. Some linked chats will also want the AI to answer on the WhatsApp side. This task adds that as an explicit, opt-in policy so a pure mirror is the default.

## Objective
Reply policy per binding: `off` (mirror only, default) | `mention` | `prefix` | `always`.

## Steps
1. `codx/junior/channels/reply_policy.py` — `should_reply(binding, event)`: `always` replies to any inbound message; `mention` requires `@codx`/`@<team user>` in the group text; `prefix` requires the message to start with `/ai`; `off` never replies.
2. When triggered, run `session.chat_with_project(chat=chat)` in a `ThreadPoolExecutor` (never inside the webhook request), one in-flight turn per binding (guard with a lock/dict; queue or drop with an "I'm still working on the previous message" notice).
3. Send a short ack ("⏳ procesando…") to the WhatsApp conversation right away; the assistant message itself goes out through the outbound sink, so no extra send code here.
4. Ignore bot-authored messages and messages already marked as mirrored (`meta_data.channel`) to avoid self-loops.
5. Surface failures as an assistant/system message in the chat and a short error to WhatsApp.

## Files
- codx/junior/channels/reply_policy.py (new)
- codx/junior/channels/bridge.py
- codx/junior/engine/chat_engine_actions.py (reuse `chat_with_project`, no rewrite)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `off` produces a pure mirror with zero AI calls (verified in tests).
- [ ] `mention`/`prefix` reply only on the expected trigger.
- [ ] Two rapid inbound messages cannot start two concurrent turns for the same binding.
- [ ] Long AI turns never block the webhook request.
